rationale: The Analysis stage showed the tertiary ED alone gives too few cases for a useful estimate, as the earlier single-site study also found (c1). All three EDs are covered by the ethics approval and the data-sharing agreement, so cases are drawn from all three sites and controls are matched within site, because program intensity differs between tertiary and community sites (c4). Incidence density sampling (c5), enrolment date as exposure (c3) and adjustment for complexity (c2) are kept. Reporting follows STROBE.
alternatives: Keep the single-site design (refused: underpowered for the effect that matters)
Pool sites without matching on site (refused: program intensity differs by site)
Before-after comparison of visit counts (refused: regression to the mean)
whyNotMoreComplex: Three sites with within-site matching is the smallest design that gives a useful estimate; adding sites outside the region would need new approvals.

decision.statement: Extend the matched case-control study to all three emergency departments, drawing cases from each site and matching four controls per case within site on age, sex and calendar month by incidence density sampling, because a single site gives too few cases and program intensity differs between sites.
decision.question: How should the case management program's association with death or ICU admission be estimated?

criteria.text: A single-site estimate would be too imprecise to inform the funding review.
Program content differs so much between sites that enrolment means different exposures.

gates.requirement: Research ethics approval covering all three emergency departments
gates.evidence: Approval REB-EM-2026-112 dated 2026-08-28 covers all three sites, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Data-sharing agreement signed by all three emergency departments
gates.evidence: Agreement DSA-2026-044 dated 2026-08-30, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Pool sites without matching on site
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c5 and on investigator-supplied approvals that cover all three sites. It replaces the single-site decision, which the investigator withdraws.

summary: Three-site matched case-control study recommended; the single-site decision is to be withdrawn.
